(Exparte)

 Judgment

The petitioner has filed the claim petition U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
That on 20.12.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, when the petitioner was proceeding as rider in a Scooter (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 bearing No.KA-09-HT-4459 along with his friend Jayashree, on Jayanagar 4th Block, 30th Cross, Bengaluru and when he reached near Cool Joint Signal, at that time all of a sudden a Goods Carrier Lorry bearing No.KA-51-B-5833 driven by its rider at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came on wrong lane and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter.

Due to impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Orthopedic Center hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein after first aid he was shifted to KVC hospital, Mysuru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient and so far he has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical,
conveyance and nourishment expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Delivery Boy and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is not able to work and not moved around properly and unable to lead a normal life as earlier and not able to do his job and suffered huge loss of income.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Goods Carrier Lorry and in this regard the Jayanagara Traffic Police have registered a (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 case against driver of the offending Goods Carrier Lorry.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending vehicle,

are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner together with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent and hence, was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent having insured the Lorry bearing No.KA-51-B-5833 (Goods Carrying Vehicle)
in terms of the Commercial Vehicle Package Policy and the same is valid as on the date of accident and the liability of this respondent is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further denied age, avocation, income of the petitioner, manner of accident, nature of the injuries sustained Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
2 by the petitioner, treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner

sentences.text:
and contended that the petitioner was riding a Motor Cycle without wearing safety headgear at the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 time of alleged accident and it is violation of M.V. Act and contended that the driver of Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident and the owner of the said vehicle allowed the driver to drove the same knowing fully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence and there is no valid permit and fitness certificate to the said lorry to ply in the public place as on the date of accident and the said lorry was converted into concrete mixer without any permission from concerned authority and in this regard the Charge sheet is filed U/Sec 52 and 177 of M.V. Act and as per records the alleged accident was taken place on 20.12.2023, but complaint was lodged on 29.12.2023 and it was a hit and run case and the lorry has been falsely implicated by creating false story and manipulated Charge sheet in order to claim unlawful gain from this respondent and hence, there is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and the compensation claimed is highly excessive and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
(SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 20.12.2023 at about 09.00 p.m, near Cool Joint Signal, near Geetha Junction Signal, Jayanagar 4th Block, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of Goods Carrier bearing registration No.KA-51-B-5833 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
06.

In order to prove his case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and got examined Medical Record Incharge and Doctors as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the respondent No.1 got examined MRO and its Legal Manager as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side evidence.
Heard both sides.

The counsel for the respondent No.1 has relied upon the citation reported in MFA No.5013/2017 (MV) in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Venkatesh Babu Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
3 and another.
09.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Venkatesh Babu Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
My findings on the aforesaid Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending goods carrier lorry by its driver, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Jayanagar (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 Traffic Police against driver of the offending goods lorry.
Ex.P.2 is Complaint shows due to rash and negligent driving of the offending goods lorry the accident was occurred and due to which the petitioner sustained injuries.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are Spot Mahazar and Sketch showing the place of accident near Cool Joint Signal Junction, Vijaya PU College, Jayanagar 4th Block,
Bengaluru, wherein the offending lorry came from East to West direction and took extreme right near Signal and Street light pole and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 and 6 are the Notices U/Sec 133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending lorry.

Ex.P.7 is Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending lorry has stated that one Raj Mohan Sheikh was driving the said lorry and he had a valid driving licence as on the date of accident and said offending lorry had valid insurance as on the date of accident.
Ex.P.8 is IMV report which discloses involvement of petitioner's Motor Cycle in the accident and more damages caused at its front side.

Ex.P.9 is Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained fracture BB (L) leg + medial malleolus fracture + posterior malleolus fracture and the doctor has opined (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 that above injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P.10 is Charge sheet shows after completion of investigation the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against driver as A1 and owner as A2 of the offending goods lorry for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.134(a & b), 187, 52 and 177 of MV Act for the reasons that the driver of the offending lorry after causing accident did not provide first aid treatment to the injured and fled away from the accident spot without stopping his vehicle and the owner of the lorry had modified the vehicle by installing a concrete pumping machine at the rear of the vehicle at the time of the accident and allowed the accused driver, A1, to drive it on a public road.
Ex.P.11 is Discharge summary shows that the petitioner sustained closed both bone fracture with tri malleolar fracture of left leg.
Ex.P.24 is IMV report which discloses involvement of offending lorry in the accident and no damages were found at the time of inspection.

The petitioner got examined Medical Records In- charge at KVC Super Speciality hospital, Mysuru,
as PW.2 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC, Case sheet and X-ray as per Ex.P.18 to 21,
Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
4 wherein it is mentioned that "Alleged H/O RTA.

He was riding a (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 two-wheeler hit by a lorry at about 09.30 p.m on 20.12.2023 near Vijaya College Signal, 4th Block,
Jayanagar, Bengaluru".

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending goods lorry and petitioner sustained injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was working as Delivery Boy and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
On account of the accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work and lost his earnings and has become permanent disabled.

12. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove his age, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.17 Driving licence.

Even though the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 16.10.1999 and the alleged accident was occurred on 20.12.2023.
Therefore, considering the said documents, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 25 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.
13.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With regard to avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 income of the petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-
and it is multiplied by 12.
14.

According to the evidence of PW.3, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained closed both bones fracture left leg and trimalleolar fracture left ankle and he assessed total disability of left lower limb at 46% and that of the whole body at 23%.
Patient is said to be a Zomoto dellivery boy and the said disabilities come in the way of his working and he has produced OPD card with examination report and X-ray as per Ex.P.22 and 23.
In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated petitioner personally.
He has not taken opinion from treated doctor and he assessed only physical disability not functional disability.
All the fractures are united and admits that petitioner without any extra support he is walking.

Trimalleloar is in ankle joint and admits that Tibia, Fibula upto ankle joint Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
5 weight bearing bones and as per Discharge summary patient condition gradually improved.

entities.text: Tibia, Fibula upto ankle joint Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now petitioner is not required any treatment.

Now implants can be removed and admits that as per guidelines 50% of the disability is not taken for a whole body and implants can be (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 removed at the government hospital and denied to the suggestion that in their hospital in cost of removing implants is Rs.8,000/- - Rs.10,000/-, witness volunteers that Rs.20,000/- to Rs.30,000/-.
However, considering the evidence of PW.3, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 18 x 15%/100 = Rs.5,18,400/-.
15.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary of KVC hospital, Mysuru, as per Ex.P.11, according to which he was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital for 04 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

16. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.9 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.3 doctor and as (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 per Case sheet, X-rays and on account of accidental injuries,
petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly with regard to fractures suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.
17. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.16,000/- p.m and he was admitted in the hospital for 04 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least two months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/-
(Rs.16,000 x 2) under this head.
18. Medical expenses:- The petitioner has produced entire Medical bills, Prescriptions and Advance receipts as per Ex.P.13 to 15 for Rs.1,50,671/-.
On perusal of Ex.P.15, Sl. Nos.3, 4, 5, 19 are included in Sl. No.6 and 20.
Hence, the excess amount of Rs.1,069/- has to be deducted in total (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 amount.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.1 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, after deducting said amount, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,49,602/- under this head.

19. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
6 20.

entities.text: Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Future medical expenses:- According to doctor PW.3 the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.50,000/- in private set up.
But he has not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.

Hence, under the facts and circumstances of the case,
the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
21. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 5,18,400-00  (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 2. Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4. Medical Expenses 1,49,602-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00
unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 32,000-00  period
7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 8,20,002-00 22.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,20,002/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

23. Regarding liability:- The counsel for respondent No.1 argued that as on the date of accident the said lorry was converted into concrete mixer without any permission from concerned authority and in this regard the Charge sheet is filed U/Sec 52 and 177 of M.V. Act and as per records the alleged accident was taken place on 20.12.2023, but complaint was lodged on 29.12.2023 and it was a hit and run case.

To prove its contention, the respondent (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 No.1 got examined MRO at Jayanagar General hospital as RW.1 and he has produced copy of MLC extract at Ex.R.2 wherein it is mentioned that "H/O RTA on 20.12.2023 at 09.00 p.m hit and run by lorry in front of Vijaya College, Jayanagar 4th Block, Bangalore".

Further, got examined its Legal Manager as RW.2 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the entire averments of the objections and in her cross-examination she admits that they have issued policy in the name of respondent No.2 organization and further admits that in Jayanagar hospital MLC document it is written as hit by lorry and stated that Police have filed false Charge sheet against lorry driver and they have not challenged the said Charge sheet and further admits that as on the date of accident the driver of lorry had valid driving licence and policy was in force.

RW.2 has produced copy of Policy as per Ex.R.4 shows as on the date of accident the policy of Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197915831/
7

entities.text: Rudresh H R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the offending lorry is valid and is in force.
On perusal of Ex.R.2, it is not given in letterhead, only put to the seal and signature of Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre.
Further, RW.2 admits that in Jayanagar hospital MLC document it is written as hit by lorry.
When the accident occurred due to rash and (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.2120/2024 negligent driving by the driver of offending lorry, the contention of respondent No.1 is not acceptable.
Therefore, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, this tribunal is the opinion that respondents No.1
and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.

Since policy of the offending goods lorry is valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

24. Issue No.3:- In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:- -
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,20,002/- (Eight lakhs twenty thousand and two rupees only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-)
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on system, corrected, initialed and then pronounced by me in open court on 04th day of February, 2026).
